title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government responds to the Committee's 2020 report on AI by outlining a strategy to strengthen public standards, including new regulations and ethical guidelines. It commits to collaborate with industry, academia, and civil society to ensure AI systems are transparent, accountable, and aligned with societal values.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual has released a policy outlining how artificial intelligence can be used within the qualifications sector, aiming to protect fairness, transparency, and academic integrity in exams and assessments. The guidance was issued in response to requests from the Secretaries of State for Education, Science, Innovation and Technology, and Business and Trade to establish clear regulatory safeguards for AI tools in certification processes.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines how copyrighted works are used to train AI systems and evaluates the legal and societal impacts of that practice. It offers guidance on balancing the rights of creators with the benefits of AI development, including suggestions for fair licensing and transparency.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The government responds to the Lords Select Committee’s report on AI in the UK, outlining its commitments to strengthen AI governance, foster innovation, and address safety and ethical concerns. It announces plans for new regulatory frameworks, increased funding for research, and measures to promote transparency and public confidence in AI systems.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: The document outlines the purpose, scope, and responsibilities of a committee tasked with examining how artificial intelligence intersects with public standards, detailing its objectives, membership, and working procedures. It also provides FAQs to clarify common questions about the committee’s mandate and how it will address policy, ethical, and regulatory considerations regarding AI in the public sector.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of AI. The submission outlines the company’s views and recommendations on how to regulate and oversee artificial intelligence.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The policy explains how AI is changing the rules that govern medical products and stresses the importance of adapting existing regulations to keep up with new AI technologies. It aims to put the AI White Paper principles into practice to ensure that medical AI tools are safe, transparent, and accountable.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy outlines a vision for the organisation to become the most effective, efficient, trusted and influential AI-driven defence body for a country of its size. It emphasises using advanced AI to strengthen operational capability, enhance decision-making, and maintain strategic advantage.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan explains how the Department for Transport will partner with the transport industry to harness the benefits of AI, such as improving efficiency and safety. It also outlines steps to identify, assess and mitigate risks, ensuring that AI deployment remains responsible and secure.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: This report outlines how copyrighted works are currently used to train and develop AI systems under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It discusses progress, challenges, and policy recommendations to balance lawful use of copyright materials with AI innovation.
